Senses.Note: The headword retains the concrete move vocabulary rather than being inflated into an unstated realization. The texts themselves qualify moves as final, upward, prior, or passed over. Apparent "one-move is..." formula hits were mostly grammatical "one who singles out the upward move" and are not self-definitions.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (宗門拈古彙集): Baofeng Bian is the exact speaker. Collected Old Cases Raised in the Lineage (宗門拈古彙集): in his explicitly introduced comment, Baofeng Bian says that old worthies take Kasyapa as holding the strategic pass and Manjusri as cutting off the ten directions, but in Baofeng's view this is precisely letting one move pass.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臨濟先鋒，放過一著。德山後令，且在一邊。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈嚴統)(第10卷-第25卷): Yunfeng Wenyue is the exact speaker. Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)): inside Yunfeng Wenyue's explicitly headed hall address, Yunfeng sets Linji's vanguard as letting one move pass and Deshan's later command aside before asking for the uniquely exposed impartial phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 生佛未興時，一著落在甚麼處？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (續燈正統): unnamed monk is the exact textual actor. Continuation of the Lamp's Orthodox Lineage (續燈正統), in Huqiu Shaolong's record. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker who asks where the single move falls before buddhas and living beings have arisen; Huqiu Shaolong answers, 'I am always intent upon this.' The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel versions in the Complete Collection of the Five Lamps and the Classified Collection of Chan Records do not name the questioning monk.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The full clause is narration or an impersonal textual proposition, not speech assigned to a rostered master.

Source text (天如惟則禪師語錄): Tianru Weize is the exact speaker. (天如惟則禪師語錄): complete-case exact-turn review identifies Tianru Weize as the actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道鴻濛未判、世界未成，者一著子落在甚麼處？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text Recorded Sayings of Baiyu (百愚禪師語錄): Baiyu Jingsi is the exact speaker. In a hall address he asks where ‘this one move’ lands before undifferentiated obscurity has divided and the world has formed.

Source text Complete Record of Master Jifei (即非禪師全錄): Jifei Ruyi is the exact verse author. The compact verse says ‘one move ahead of the mechanism’ and follows it with not yielding when responsibility is present.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：我有這一著，人人口裏嚼。嚼得破者，速須吐却。嚼不破者，翻成毒藥。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): Zhihai Benyi is the exact hall speaker, calling this “one move” something everyone chews and warning that failure to break through it turns it into poison.

Senses.Explanation: A single move, play, or stroke is one deliberate action within an encounter. Chan speakers use the counting phrase for getting a move in first, reserving a final move, missing one move, or demanding the move that changes the situation. The game-like noun appears in recurring Chan compounds: "let one move pass" (放過一著, 617 occurrences), "the final move" (末後一著, 104), "the upward move" (向上一著, 279), "one move ahead" (先一著, 38), and the suffixed "one move" (一著子, 601). A case-comment collection appraises an earlier response as "precisely letting one move pass," then adds "danger" (正是放過一著；險). A lamp address pairs "Linji's vanguard—let one move pass" with "Deshan's later command—set it aside" (臨濟先鋒，放過一著；德山後令，且在一邊). Questions ask, "before living beings and buddhas arose, where did one move fall?" (生佛未興時，一著落在甚麼處). Feiyin says, "present one move face to face; the person concerned must personally take it up" (覿面提持個一著，當人要在親領略). These uses support the ordinary move/play sense while showing its Chan deployment as question, appraisal, sequence, and named move.
